subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 12-year-old boy is evaluated for painless hematuria that has persisted for 2 years and has recently been accompanied by proteinuria. He has bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and an anterior lenticonus on slit-lamp examination. His maternal uncle began dialysis at age 30, and two male cousins have similar urine findings.
question: Which of the following proteins is most likely defective in this patient?
explanation_correct: This patient has Alport syndrome, most often an X-linked disorder caused by mutations in COL4A5 that encodes the alpha-5 chain of type IV collagen. Type IV collagen is the major structural component of basement membranes, including the glomerular basement membrane, the cochlea, and the lens capsule, which explains the combination of hematuria, sensorineural hearing loss, and anterior lenticonus. The male-to-male sparing inheritance pattern with affected maternal uncles is typical of X-linked disease.

explanation_incorrect.A: Type I collagen defects cause osteogenesis imperfecta with bone fragility and blue sclerae, not progressive nephritis and hearing loss.
explanation_incorrect.B: Type II collagen is found in cartilage, the vitreous body, and the nucleus pulposus; its defects do not cause the renal and cochlear findings described.
explanation_incorrect.C: Type III collagen (reticulin) defects cause the vascular form of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome with arterial and bowel rupture.
explanation_incorrect.D: Fibrillin-1 defects cause Marfan syndrome with tall stature, ectopia lentis, and aortic root dilation, not hematuria with hearing loss.

educationalObjective: Alport syndrome is caused by defective type IV collagen (most often COL4A5) of basement membranes, producing hematuria, sensorineural hearing loss, and anterior lenticonus.
